references_named: Alfred H. Barr Jr., Cubism and Abstract Art flowchart (MoMA, 1936)
rationale: The mechanism is the argument: native indeterminate <progress> elements are spec-obliged to animate striving toward a finish they are never given, so the modernist teleology (Greenberg/Barr) is performed rather than illustrated. Leaving the widget unstyled (no appearance:none) makes the browser/OS the author of the look, a clean Duchampian readymade move. The prefers-reduced-motion freeze is a genuinely witty double-coding: accessibility default doubles as the punchline. Build is minimal and honest — declarative markup, one timer, no storage, no network. Distinct from the catalogue: no prior work targets the indeterminate-progress gesture or the Greenberg/Barr modernist-progress myth specifically.
reservations: The narrative link to the twenty-year argument is somewhat thin — it answers a discourse (modernist teleology) rather than a specific prior y-a-v-a work, though it sits comfortably on the chance/order-adjacent axis of 'behaviour over artifact.' The 'six movements' list is illustrative scaffolding rather than load-bearing mechanism; a single indeterminate bar would carry the idea equally well, which slightly dilutes P3's restraint.
revision_suggestion: Consider whether the six-bar list earns its keep or whether a single indeterminate bar with the same caption lands the joke more sharply; if kept, the movements could be chosen to rhyme with prior catalogue entries (e.g., one Suprematist, one readymade) to tighten the lineage.
